from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Real-World Filtering", ["Frequencies identify specific sound types.", "Unwanted noise has unique high frequencies.", "Remove these to clear your audio."])
        
        # Load assets
        mic = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microphone.svg")
        comp = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg")
        
        # Create graphs
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}, x_length=4, y_length=2)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Signal function (noisy)
        noisy_signal = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(10 * x), color='#FF0000')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color('#FF0000')
        self.place_at_grid(mic, 'B2', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(axes, noisy_signal, mic)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color('#FFFFFF')
        # Represent low-pass filter (shaded box)
        filter_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=2, color='#FFFFFF', fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(filter_box, 'C4', 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(filter_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color('#00FF00')
        cleaned_signal = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color='#00FF00')
        self.place_at_grid(comp, 'B5', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Transform(noisy_signal, cleaned_signal), FadeOut(filter_box), FadeIn(comp))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie can be deconstructed into its original ingredients, any complex signal can be broken down into simple sine waves.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Berry-Banana-Kale' smoothie being separated back into three distinct piles of fruit.

sections.title: Prerequisite Recap: Rotating Vectors (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Briefly revisit Euler’s Formula (e^ix = cos x + i sin x). Explain how a signal can be visualized as a point rotating around a circle at different frequencies.
sections.example: An animation of a vector spinning; the 'shadow' cast on the X-axis creates a sine wave.

sections.title: The Mechanism: The Center of Mass (1:30-3:00)
sections.content: Explain the Fourier Transform as a tool that 'wraps' a signal around a center point at a specific frequency. If the frequency matches the signal's component, the center of mass shifts away from the origin.
sections.example: A complex wave of a chirping bird 'wrapped' around a circle. When the rotation speed matches the bird's pitch, the center of mass spikes—revealing the frequency.

sections.title: Key Concept: Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain (3:00-4:00)
sections.content: Contrast the Time Domain (where things happen) with the Frequency Domain (what things are made of). Emphasize that the Fourier Transform is the bridge between these two views.
sections.example: Side-by-side animation: A piano keyboard playing a chord (Time Domain) vs. a bar chart showing the specific notes being played (Frequency Domain).

sections.title: Application: Real-World Filtering (4:00-5:00)
sections.content: Demonstrate why this matters. If we can see the frequencies, we can remove the ones we don't want (Noise Cancellation).
sections.example: A smartphone character filtering out 'background construction noise' from a voice recording by simply erasing the high-frequency spikes in the Frequency Domain.
